scope: Proposition 6.2 (Packing-preserving sparsification) of the manuscript “The strong thin tree conjecture” (preprints/The-strong-thin-tree-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 174 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a2b847ce72f66109), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an absolute integer rstep such that the following holds for every integer r ≥ rstep. If H has at least two vertices and contains r edge-disjoint spanning trees, set u = r−1/16 , q = ⌊(1 − u)r⌋, ϵ = 6r−1/2 , τ = 2 √ ϵ + ϵ. Then H has a spanning subgraph H′ containing at least (6.2) r′ = ⌊ (1 − 4u)r 2 ⌋ edge-disjoint spanning trees, such that every nonempty proper S ⊂ V (H) satisfies (6.3) |δH′ (S)| ≤ ( 1 2 + 3τ ) |δH(S)|. The cutoff may be chosen so that, in addition, (6.4) 5 16 ≤ r′ r ≤ 1 2 , 1 2 + 3τ r′/r ≤ 1 + 15u.
